top.title: Tinubu to Nigerians: I promise better future
top.description: •Says, I share your pain, we’re out of dark tunnel •Knocks Atiku, Obi in Uyo, approves Ibom Deep Sea Port •Bus conveying women to welcome President crashes By Egufe Yafugborhi UYO — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu yesterday promised a better future for Nigerians even as he took a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), declaring that they lacked the leadership qualities to govern Nigeria. His visit, however, was overshadowed by a road crash involving an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome him, in which one person was feared dead and several others sustained serious injuries. top.title: CBN updates guidelines for stablecoins operation
top.description: •Sets N15bn capital requirement By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria has issued guidelines for virtual asset providers in the country, setting minimum capital requirement of N10 billion and N15 billion for Classes 1 and 2 issuers, respectively. This was contained in a circular with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, date November 5, 2026 and signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Mr. Musa Jimoh. According to the bank, “A Class 1 Licensed Issuer shall maintain paid-up capital of N10 billion Naira or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. Class 2 Licensed Issuer shall maintain minimum paid-up capital of N15 billion or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. “Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital.” Class 2 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against foreign currencies, including the US dollar, while Class 1 refers to issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins. CBN said the emergence of virtual assets, stablecoins, and tokenised payment instruments “presents significant opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlement, and digital commerce,” but that, “their growing adoption also introduces risks relating to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, illicit finance, operational resilience, and foreign exchange management.” It added that the guidelines were issued pursuant to its statutory mandate to promote monetary and financial stability and regulate Nigeria’s payments system. “These Guidelines establish a risk-based framework for the licensing, regulation, supervision, and oversight of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs), and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). “These Guidelines seek to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability, and efficiency of the Nigerian financial system. “These Guidelines also seek to provide regulatory requirements relating to governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, AML/CFT/CPF compliance, and reporting obligations for entities and persons engaged in regulated non-security virtual asset activities within or involving Nigeria,” the bank explained. The CBN’s updated framework outlines clear boundaries for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), with a sharp focus on foreign exchange liquidity, consumer protection, and peer-to-peer (P2P) trading identity protocols. top.description: Eian Elmer #55 of the Wisconsin Badgers dribbles the basketball while being defended by Kam Martin #2 of the Denver Pioneers at Kohl Center in Madison, Wisconsin, on November 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers beat the Delaware Blue Hens 73-64 on Friday to improve to 2-0, just days after beating the Denver Pioneers 75-68 in their season opener on Monday. Now, Monday’s game was more of a struggle for the Badgers, with things getting within single digits in the final minutes. This game wasn’t as close as the score implied at the end, with Wisconsin holding a comfortable double-digit lead for most of the last seven minutes. But the Badgers look like a major work in progress through two games, as they sort things out with their new-look roster. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s 73-64 win over Delaware on Friday evening. Offense too stagnant early The Badgers got off to this one shooting a ton of threes, with Braeden Carrington, Nolan Winter, and Eian Elmer all connecting from deep. But as the first half went along and Delaware kept things close, the Badgers became far too stagnant on offense. While the ball was moving around, Wisconsin did not attack the basket until late in the shot clock, instead passing around the perimeter looking for threes. It was far too passive an outlook, while Delaware was looking to be aggressive and take the game to Wisconsin on the other end. Owen Foxwell was the only one initiating by attacking, and those actions alone set up a couple of open shots and looks at the rim. Foxwell had four assists, but could not get his rhythm as a scorer, going 1 for 5 from the field, while splitting his lone pair of free throws. In the second half, we saw Foxwell attack more and end up with 13 points in the half alone, working well from the free-throw line. But as a team, that has to be more consistently happening to set up the threes, not the other way around. This could also be partly because of a new group of players settling in together. Guys are still figuring out their spots and with that has been some passive play to start the season. Eian Elmer’s aggressiveness Eian Elmer is going to be a big part of this team’s success this year. The Badgers are going to need him to step up and potentially take over as their top scorer, with Foxwell being their top facilitator. He had 18 points on 13 shots in the opener, and I thought there were times he was too hesitant in this one after popping a few early threes. Elmer took a poor three later in the first half from too deep, and all of his field goal makes were from beyond the arc on Friday. The Badgers need more initiators alongside Foxwell, and Elmer is the guy who’s going to have to step up from that group. top.description: •Judgement that gave Uzodimma governorship victory fingered By Ikechukwu Nnochiri A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Read Also : Uzodinma sworn-in as sixth governor of Imo Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. Votes counted in courtroom The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. top.title: Saban Slams 24-Team Playoff, Says It’s “Too Many”
top.description: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Nick Saban talks to the media at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Nick Saban cut right through the noise on Friday when he called the new 24-team playoff a bad idea . The former Alabama coach told fans on the “New Heights” podcast that the field is simply too crowded. He believes the expansion hurts the game more than it helps. Saban made his point clear while talking to the Kelce brothers about the changes coming next season. The core issue is that the best teams will still win, but the rest will just play for cash. Saban argued that the current system already stretched players too thin with extra games. He noted that his teams played 15 games three times and he thought that was too many, according to Yahoo Sports . Now the plan adds even more pressure without fixing the quality of the competition. Money Is The Only Reason When Travis Kelce asked Saban why anyone would push for a bigger tournament, the answer was blunt. “So what is the reason to actually do it?” Saban asked the audience on the Friday podcast. Jason Kelce answered immediately, saying, “Money.” Saban agreed with the assessment but warned fans about the cost of that cash. He hates to see the SEC championship game go away because it means so much to the players and fans. That tradition is a big thing for the league, and it is a great venue that people love. The new rules mean conference title games will likely disappear to make room for the expanded playoff. As part of the agreement, a Big Ten squad must face a power opponent in a non-conference matchup. Should conference titles remain, a team might compete in 18 contests upon advancing to the national title. Dropping the title games allows the playoffs to start earlier and caps the total number of games at 17. Saban feels this is still too much for college athletes to handle. Tradition Gets Lost For A Deal The College Football Playoff issued a statement on Friday afternoon about the media rights for this expansion. The statement said, “A formal agreement between the CFP and ESPN regarding future media rights in connection with potential expansion is in the final stages of review by the CFP.” This confirms the deal is moving forward despite the complaints from the coaching ranks. Saban thinks the system would have worked fine with just 12 or maybe 16 teams. He said the 12-team version was a good tournament even if a few teams that should not have been in got selected. The SEC already has a nine-game schedule in place to match the other power conferences. This rule forces teams to play tougher opponents without the safety net of a conference title game. Saban believes pride in winning a conference championship matters more than adding weak teams to a bracket. He thinks the political pressure to make the field bigger led to a flawed plan. The former coach knows that 24 teams are too many for a true national championship race.

top.title: ‘Someone Tell Brittany Mahomes,’ ‘Argument Over’ — NFL Fans React to Jason, Travis Kelce Taking Refs’ Side in Controversial Call During Broncos-Chiefs
top.description: Jason Kelce, Brittany Mahomes and Travis Kelce Even with one of them in a Kansas City Chiefs uniform, Jason and Travis Kelce sided with the officials. On Wednesday’s episode of “New Heights,” the brothers agreed with the false start called on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore that wiped out Patrick Mahomes’ would-be winning touchdown pass in Week 8’s 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. However, that put the brothers on the other side of the call from Brittany Mahomes, who blasted it in an Instagram story after the game. NFL fans reacting to the clip treated the brothers’ take as the final word, with some of them also asking Patrick Mahomes’ wife to take notice. NFL Fans React as Travis and Jason Kelce Weigh In On Officiating Debate Trailing 28-24, the Chiefs drove from their own 44, and Mahomes’ 1-yard touchdown throw to Rashee Rice looked like the winner until Moore’s flag erased it. On the replay, Moore’s hips shift slightly as he turns his head toward Mahomes. At the same instant, right guard Trey Smith, who had been looking back toward the quarterback before the snap, swings his own head forward. Pushed back 5 yards to the 6, Kansas City replayed fourth down, and Malcolm Roach’s sack of Mahomes ended the game. Brittany wrote that night: “You can’t tell me you call that on a game-winning TD, oh wait, yeah, I can, ’cause it’s us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can’t tell me otherwise.” Three days later, the Kelce brothers broke down the same play and reached a different conclusion. “I’m going to go on record and say that this is definitely a penalty,” Jason said, as Travis agreed, “Yeah, he flinches.” Fans who agreed with the officials now had the brothers’ words to point to, and Brittany’s name came up more than once. “Someone tell Brittany Mahomes,” one fan wrote. top.title: Greenwich girls volleyball beats Trumbull to win second straight FCIAC championship
top.description: Greenwich celebrates winning the FCIAC volleyball championship over Trumbull at Stamford High School in Stamford on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Scott Ericson/Hearst Connecticut Media) STAMFORD - The top-seeded Greenwich girls volleyball team made it two in a row, beating No. 2 Trumbull 3-1 (25-21, 25-27, 25-22, 25-13) Friday night at Stamford High to claim back-to-back FCIAC championships. It is the fifth overall championship for the Cardinals, who remained unbeaten (20-0) heading into the CIAC tournament. "It's so exciting and such an amazing feeling, and I am so proud of my whole team," Greenwich junior libero Bailee Dayon said. "I think we set up a very great block the last two sets and it made it easier for me to read." Dayon was in fact able to read the Trumbull attack well, recording 27 digs in the match to go along with 13 assists and 15 service points, many of which came when Greenwich needed them the most. "(Dayon) is just great all the time," Greenwich coach Marianna Linnehan said. "She is fantastic. That girl can just dig every ball. When Mckenzyi (Bell of Trumbull) was in the front row, she was killing us and we really fixed that in the last two sets." For Greenwich, Kayah Armstrong had 20 kills and two blocks, Heidi Zieme had 16 digs and 14 kills, Victoria Sullivan had 15 digs and 25 assists, and Beatriz Lisboa Da Cunha De Freitas had 20 assists and nine digs. Bell was stellar all night at the net for Trumbull, delivering 17 kills. "I thought sets one through three we did exactly what we had to do, but in set four, we kind of ran out of steam a bit," Trumbull coach Nicole Trommelen said. "It was fun for a big stretch of that game watching Mckenzyi go." After splitting the first two sets, Trumbull (19-2) led most of the third until Greenwich took its first lead at 21-20. Trumbull's only loss of the regular season came to Greenwich. Those were the only two sets Greenwich dropped during the regular season in going unbeaten. Greenwich will be the No. 1 seed in the Class LL tournament, which begins next week, while Trumbull will be the No. 3 seed. Both teams have first-round byes and will begin play in the second round Nov. 12. Player of the Game Sammie Tommasino, Greenwich : In a sea of talented players, Tommasino earned MVP honors with 13 digs, 15 kills, two blocks and 10 service points. Quotable "We worked so hard for this. We were expecting a tough game but we knew we could do it because we had so much passion and we really wanted it. It's the most fun thing ever to play with this team." - Sammie Tommasino. Greenwich 3, Trumbull 1 TRUMBULL 21 27 22 13 GREENWICH 25 25 25 25 Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. top.title: UNC dominates behind Terrence Brown in win over Wofford
top.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first UNC basketball game of the season may have felt like uneasy dental work with a happy ending after the Tar Heels managed to do just enough to beat Western Carolina. Friday night against Wofford was a different story. As in their first game, the Tar Heels never trailed. What was different, though, was that the Tar Heels looked the part as they overpowered the Terriers on their way to a 109-70 win. It was the highest point total for the Tar Heels since November of 2018. Carolina’s offense definitely came easier in this one with five players ending up in double figures. Michael Malone continued his five in, five out strategy playing with an A/B lineup. Terrence Brown was very good for the A group, leading the team with 21 points. Jaydon Young, Alex Samodurov, and Maximo Adams all turned in strong performances for the B side. They finished with 15, 13, and 11 points, respectively. Adams led the team in rebounds with 11. The bench was responsible for 58 of the Tar Heels’ points. Jarin Stevenson was the other Tar Heel in double figures with 10 points. If it weren’t for the efforts of Cutter Sisk for Wofford, the final score would have been even more lopsided. He was responsible for 27 of the Terriers’ points. He was 11-18 from the field and grabbed seven boards to lead Wofford. The Terriers got the best of the Heels on the offensive glass, 17-14, but the Heels converted more second-chance points, 19-10. The overall rebounding margin was still too close for comfort with UNC holding a +7 mark in the category, but almost everything else was so lopsided that it didn’t become a major factor. The Heels shot 52% from the field and made 10 of their three-point attempts. They also converted on 23 of their 29 free throw attempts. Seven steals for the Heels helped lead to 13 turnovers for Wofford. Carolina turned those into 14 points on the other end. After a couple nail-biter exhibition game and a too-close-for-comfort start to the season, it was very good to get a comfortable win. It was also great to see that success was spread across so much of the lineup. Hopefully this was the game that gets Brown fully going, and Adams looked very impressive as a freshman playing in just his second game. Depth has not been a reliable feature at times in recent memory for Carolina, but the team showed tonight that there are more than a few guys who can step up and put points on the board. Carolina tries to keep it rolling on Tuesday when they welcome Wyoming to Chapel Hill.

top.title: FSU moves to 2-0 with 23-point win over Troy
top.description: Florida State began 2-0 for the second straight season under head coach Luke Loucks, taking down the Troy Trojans 91-68 in the Seminoles’ home opener. Marcis Ponder had a second straight double-double, with 10 points and 10 rebounds, while Shon Abaev led all scorers with 20 points. Sebastian Rancik had 18 points and three rebounds, going a perfect 8-for-8 from the charity stripe. Florida State started hot, shooting out to a 12-2 lead, but then an offensive drought saw the Seminoles stall out. FSU took its largest lead to that point at the 12:45 mark, going up 17-5 off a Kameron Taylor three, but the momentum was lost as Florida State struggled to hit anything from the field — though a strong performance on the glass helped mitigate those shooting woes. The Seminoles made just two baskets over the next eight minutes, going 2-for-14 before a Rancik three-ball. FSU proceeded to go on a 10-2 run to close out the half, pushing its lead to 14 before a late three from Troy made it a 37-26 game at the close of the first. Marcis Ponder fought through contact for another and-one, hitting the free throw to make it a 58-44 game with 11:24 left. That lead ballooned to 17 at 7:34 on an Abaev three, and it would hover around that mark for the next four minutes before hitting 21 after a pair of Rancik free throws. FSU emptied the bench with 1:24 on the clock, with Martay Barnes hitting a jumper with 37 seconds left to make it a 91-68 game, which would hold as the final score. nigeria.title: CBN updates guidelines for stablecoins operation
nigeria.description: •Sets N15bn capital requirement By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria has issued guidelines for virtual asset providers in the country, setting minimum capital requirement of N10 billion and N15 billion for Classes 1 and 2 issuers, respectively. This was contained in a circular with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, date November 5, 2026 and signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Mr. Musa Jimoh. According to the bank, “A Class 1 Licensed Issuer shall maintain paid-up capital of N10 billion Naira or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. Class 2 Licensed Issuer shall maintain minimum paid-up capital of N15 billion or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. “Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital.” Class 2 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against foreign currencies, including the US dollar, while Class 1 refers to issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins. CBN said the emergence of virtual assets, stablecoins, and tokenised payment instruments “presents significant opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlement, and digital commerce,” but that, “their growing adoption also introduces risks relating to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, illicit finance, operational resilience, and foreign exchange management.” It added that the guidelines were issued pursuant to its statutory mandate to promote monetary and financial stability and regulate Nigeria’s payments system. “These Guidelines establish a risk-based framework for the licensing, regulation, supervision, and oversight of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs), and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). “These Guidelines seek to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability, and efficiency of the Nigerian financial system. “These Guidelines also seek to provide regulatory requirements relating to governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, AML/CFT/CPF compliance, and reporting obligations for entities and persons engaged in regulated non-security virtual asset activities within or involving Nigeria,” the bank explained. The CBN’s updated framework outlines clear boundaries for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), with a sharp focus on foreign exchange liquidity, consumer protection, and peer-to-peer (P2P) trading identity protocols. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. nigeria.title: The Obidient Pulse: Obi Warns Against Uncertainty As Opposition Groups Face A Test Of Unity

Obi reacts to court ruling affecting ADC The Federal High Court in Abuja has nullified the leadership of the African Democratic Congress under Senator David Mark and set aside the party’s processes, including the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate. The ADC says it will appeal. Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, described the ruling as “unsettling and surprising”. He said there should be certainty about parties and candidates ahead of an election and called for opposition politics to be protected. Obi also accused the ruling APC of engineering the instability, an allegation the party rejected. The court decision concerns the ADC; it does not directly affect Obi’s NDC candidacy. Court fight places opposition unity under pressure The ADC has rejected the judgment and says it will challenge it in court. Atiku has also said he will appeal and seek a stay of execution. The case now puts the spotlight on the judiciary’s role in resolving internal party disputes and on whether opposition parties can maintain stable platforms as the election approaches. Disagreement among Obi’s support groups continues The court ruling comes amid public friction between the OK Movement and leaders of the Obidient Movement and NDC campaign. The OK Movement accused them of fuelling divisions; the NDC campaign dismissed the dispute as a distraction, while the Obidient coordinator’s aide said he was focused on mobilising support for Obi. The exchanges raise a practical question for the campaign: can its different support groups coordinate their work, clarify who speaks for whom and build lasting grassroots organisation? The public disagreements are a reminder that a broad support base needs clear roles and disciplined coordination to turn enthusiasm into effective political mobilisation. The task ahead For the Obidient Movement, the immediate challenge is to keep attention on voters, organisation and the issues facing Nigerians. The movement’s strength will be measured not only by the size of its support, but by how effectively it organises that support across communities and sustains a credible campaign. In a political season increasingly shaped by court cases and internal disputes, the demand from supporters is likely to be simple: less public quarrelling, clearer communication and visible work on the ground. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . business.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s 73-64 win over Delaware on Friday evening. Offense too stagnant early The Badgers got off to this one shooting a ton of threes, with Braeden Carrington, Nolan Winter, and Eian Elmer all connecting from deep. But as the first half went along and Delaware kept things close, the Badgers became far too stagnant on offense. While the ball was moving around, Wisconsin did not attack the basket until late in the shot clock, instead passing around the perimeter looking for threes. It was far too passive an outlook, while Delaware was looking to be aggressive and take the game to Wisconsin on the other end. Owen Foxwell was the only one initiating by attacking, and those actions alone set up a couple of open shots and looks at the rim. sports.title: Saban Slams 24-Team Playoff, Says It’s “Too Many”
sports.description: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Nick Saban talks to the media at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Nick Saban cut right through the noise on Friday when he called the new 24-team playoff a bad idea . The former Alabama coach told fans on the “New Heights” podcast that the field is simply too crowded. He believes the expansion hurts the game more than it helps. Saban made his point clear while talking to the Kelce brothers about the changes coming next season. The core issue is that the best teams will still win, but the rest will just play for cash. Saban argued that the current system already stretched players too thin with extra games. He noted that his teams played 15 games three times and he thought that was too many, according to Yahoo Sports . Now the plan adds even more pressure without fixing the quality of the competition. Money Is The Only Reason When Travis Kelce asked Saban why anyone would push for a bigger tournament, the answer was blunt. “So what is the reason to actually do it?” Saban asked the audience on the Friday podcast. Jason Kelce answered immediately, saying, “Money.” Saban agreed with the assessment but warned fans about the cost of that cash. He hates to see the SEC championship game go away because it means so much to the players and fans. That tradition is a big thing for the league, and it is a great venue that people love. The new rules mean conference title games will likely disappear to make room for the expanded playoff. As part of the agreement, a Big Ten squad must face a power opponent in a non-conference matchup. Should conference titles remain, a team might compete in 18 contests upon advancing to the national title. Dropping the title games allows the playoffs to start earlier and caps the total number of games at 17. Saban feels this is still too much for college athletes to handle. Tradition Gets Lost For A Deal The College Football Playoff issued a statement on Friday afternoon about the media rights for this expansion. The statement said, “A formal agreement between the CFP and ESPN regarding future media rights in connection with potential expansion is in the final stages of review by the CFP.” This confirms the deal is moving forward despite the complaints from the coaching ranks. Saban thinks the system would have worked fine with just 12 or maybe 16 teams. He said the 12-team version was a good tournament even if a few teams that should not have been in got selected. The SEC already has a nine-game schedule in place to match the other power conferences. This rule forces teams to play tougher opponents without the safety net of a conference title game. Saban believes pride in winning a conference championship matters more than adding weak teams to a bracket. He thinks the political pressure to make the field bigger led to a flawed plan. The former coach knows that 24 teams are too many for a true national championship race.

It is the fifth overall championship for the Cardinals, who remained unbeaten (20-0) heading into the CIAC tournament. "It's so exciting and such an amazing feeling, and I am so proud of my whole team," Greenwich junior libero Bailee Dayon said. "I think we set up a very great block the last two sets and it made it easier for me to read." Dayon was in fact able to read the Trumbull attack well, recording 27 digs in the match to go along with 13 assists and 15 service points, many of which came when Greenwich needed them the most. "(Dayon) is just great all the time," Greenwich coach Marianna Linnehan said. "She is fantastic. That girl can just dig every ball. For Greenwich, Kayah Armstrong had 20 kills and two blocks, Heidi Zieme had 16 digs and 14 kills, Victoria Sullivan had 15 digs and 25 assists, and Beatriz Lisboa Da Cunha De Freitas had 20 assists and nine digs. "It was fun for a big stretch of that game watching Mckenzyi go." After splitting the first two sets, Trumbull (19-2) led most of the third until Greenwich took its first lead at 21-20. sports.title: UNC dominates behind Terrence Brown in win over Wofford
sports.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first UNC basketball game of the season may have felt like uneasy dental work with a happy ending after the Tar Heels managed to do just enough to beat Western Carolina. Friday night against Wofford was a different story. As in their first game, the Tar Heels never trailed. What was different, though, was that the Tar Heels looked the part as they overpowered the Terriers on their way to a 109-70 win. It was the highest point total for the Tar Heels since November of 2018. Carolina’s offense definitely came easier in this one with five players ending up in double figures. Michael Malone continued his five in, five out strategy playing with an A/B lineup. Terrence Brown was very good for the A group, leading the team with 21 points. Jaydon Young, Alex Samodurov, and Maximo Adams all turned in strong performances for the B side. They finished with 15, 13, and 11 points, respectively. Adams led the team in rebounds with 11. The bench was responsible for 58 of the Tar Heels’ points. Jarin Stevenson was the other Tar Heel in double figures with 10 points. If it weren’t for the efforts of Cutter Sisk for Wofford, the final score would have been even more lopsided. He was responsible for 27 of the Terriers’ points. He was 11-18 from the field and grabbed seven boards to lead Wofford. The Terriers got the best of the Heels on the offensive glass, 17-14, but the Heels converted more second-chance points, 19-10. The overall rebounding margin was still too close for comfort with UNC holding a +7 mark in the category, but almost everything else was so lopsided that it didn’t become a major factor. The Heels shot 52% from the field and made 10 of their three-point attempts. They also converted on 23 of their 29 free throw attempts. Seven steals for the Heels helped lead to 13 turnovers for Wofford. Carolina turned those into 14 points on the other end. After a couple nail-biter exhibition game and a too-close-for-comfort start to the season, it was very good to get a comfortable win. It was also great to see that success was spread across so much of the lineup. Hopefully this was the game that gets Brown fully going, and Adams looked very impressive as a freshman playing in just his second game. Depth has not been a reliable feature at times in recent memory for Carolina, but the team showed tonight that there are more than a few guys who can step up and put points on the board. Carolina tries to keep it rolling on Tuesday when they welcome Wyoming to Chapel Hill.

sports.description: Florida State began 2-0 for the second straight season under head coach Luke Loucks, taking down the Troy Trojans 91-68 in the Seminoles’ home opener. Marcis Ponder had a second straight double-double, with 10 points and 10 rebounds, while Shon Abaev led all scorers with 20 points. Sebastian Rancik had 18 points and three rebounds, going a perfect 8-for-8 from the charity stripe. Florida State started hot, shooting out to a 12-2 lead, but then an offensive drought saw the Seminoles stall out. FSU took its largest lead to that point at the 12:45 mark, going up 17-5 off a Kameron Taylor three, but the momentum was lost as Florida State struggled to hit anything from the field — though a strong performance on the glass helped mitigate those shooting woes. The Seminoles made just two baskets over the next eight minutes, going 2-for-14 before a Rancik three-ball. FSU proceeded to go on a 10-2 run to close out the half, pushing its lead to 14 before a late three from Troy made it a 37-26 game at the close of the first. The Seminoles would stay ahead by double digits for the next four minutes before the Trojans cut it down to nine at the 13-minute mark off an and-one play. Each time Troy had a moment, though, the Seminoles responded — first with an and-one of their own, then with a nice jumper from Abaev after a Troy three. Marcis Ponder fought through contact for another and-one, hitting the free throw to make it a 58-44 game with 11:24 left. That lead ballooned to 17 at 7:34 on an Abaev three, and it would hover around that mark for the next four minutes before hitting 21 after a pair of Rancik free throws. FSU emptied the bench with 1:24 on the clock, with Martay Barnes hitting a jumper with 37 seconds left to make it a 91-68 game, which would hold as the final score. Next up for Florida State is a home matchup against the No. 1 Florida Gators next Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 6 p.m. (ESPN2). sports.title: Wei Lin leads Oregon men's basketball's rout of Eastern Washington
sports.description: The strength of the Oregon men’s basketball team will be its depth and its roster of interchangeable parts, interim coach Tony Stubblefield has declared on several occasions the past month. On Nov. 6, it was Wei Lin’s turn to claim the spotlight. The junior reserve point guard, one of just two returning players for the Ducks, had 20 points to lead Oregon to a 98-71 nonconference rout of Eastern Washington on Friday afternoon in Matthew Knight Arena. Lin's point total was his second highest in 32 games at Oregon (2-0) and three points shy of his career high – a 23-point performance in overtime against Rutgers last season. “He really provided a big spark for us off the bench,” Stubblefield said. Lin finished 7 for 9 from the field, 3 for 5 from 3-point range, and had four rebounds, three steals and just two turnovers in 21 minutes. One of his turnovers was the result of an errant behind-the-back-pass attempt on a fast break Lin started with a steal late in the second half. “Wei has really put in the work,” Stubblefield said. “He’s very coachable and it looks like he’s gotten better from last year. He’s defending harder and being more of an all-around basketball player. … And he’s taking better shots." Lin wasn’t the only Duck to impress on offense. Fred Payne had 16 points and was 4 for 6 from 3-point range, Pharoah Compton scored 13 and was 6 for 6 from the field and Malique Ewin had 10 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. Oregon shot 60% from the field (39 for 65) for the second game in a row, had 26 assists and won the rebounding battle 38-24. The Ducks were up 53-39 at halftime and only trailed for 22 seconds the entire game. And just like in their season-opening win against Montana last Monday, the Ducks entertained with their athleticism and ability to play above the rim, especially on the fast break. “During the recruiting process, that was something we really looked for,” Stubblefield said. “Getting back to our athleticism, improving our athleticism. So we had a good idea what we were getting with these young men, but they’ve been great to work with.” Oregon will be without guard Tyrone Riley IV until December Oregon played Friday without junior guard Tyrone Riley IV, who sustained a left hand injury against Montana and will be out for at least four weeks. He was on the bench Friday with a wrap on his thumb. The transfer from San Francisco had a team-high 17 points against the Grizzlies, along with four steals, three assists and two blocks. Stubblefield called it a "fluke injury" and added that "we got guys over there that are ready to step up and we'll be OK until he gets back." Jasper Johnson replaced him in the starting lineup against Eastern Washington and had six points, one assist and four turnovers. What’s next for Oregon men’s basketball? sports.title: ‘This is sad’: Criticism mounts as Dianna Russini makes media return after Mike Vrabel scandal
sports.description: Dianna Russini Dianna Russini appears to be on the verge of returning to NFL media. Her new home, however, has raised plenty of eyebrows. The former NFL insider is reportedly set to host a new weekly show with BetUS, an offshore sportsbook based in Costa Rica. Many people on social media weren’t sure what to make of that choice, especially considering the NFL’s stance on unregulated gambling. Russini’s reported return Russini resigned from her role as a senior NFL insider at The Athletic in April after photos surfaced that suggested a years-long romantic relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Both denied any wrongdoing, though The Athletic later released an internal review that called the relationship a “clear violation” of its standards. Now, it appears that Russini has found her next gig. Front Office Sports reported that she was likely to launch a digital show sponsored by a sportsbook, with BetUS emerging as the frontrunner, according to Ryan Glasspiegel, Mark Maske, and Michael McCarthy . BetUS has since teased the arrival of “a familiar voice” for a live weekly NFL show that will debut on Wednesday, Nov. 11, per Awful Announcing’s Sean Keeley . The show will reportedly feature game previews, guest interviews, and betting picks, and the host will also write a weekly column. The company plans to reveal the host on Monday, but an X account called “Russini Report” had already been promoting a live NFL show on Wednesdays. That page previously said the show was “powered by BetUS,” before the wording was removed, according to FOS. As Awful Announcing’s Brendon Kleen noted , the show will be a major test of whether Russini can still break news and draw an audience following the Vrabel scandal. Reactions Plenty of people, including some who cover the sports betting industry, questioned whether partnering with an offshore sportsbook was the right move for Russini. “For someone who has so carefully calibrated her reemergence, partnering with an offshore sportsbook while trying to rebuild NFL ties is a curious choice. The league has made its hostility to unregulated sports gambling abundantly clear. See league’s stance on prediction markets,” wrote sports betting attorney Daniel Wallach . “Over/Under on the % of people who don’t know that BetUS is an offshore sports book … 90%?” wrote Matt Perrault , host of The Bostonian vs. The Book . “Chat, is working for an offshore sportsbook a step up from being caught f***ing your interview subjects?” wrote sports betting reporter Sam McQuillan . “Russini does not have good people in her corner. This is sad,” wrote the popular NFL betting analyst Jeff Sunday . Needless to say, Russini’s new show will have plenty of eyes on it when it debuts next week. technology.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
technology.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. technology.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
technology.description: Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes. The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times . Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region. Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region's undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. It's not surprising to me that you can get to it, but how little effort you need to put into setting that up to get models to share anything.” The researchers tested nine models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Luna, and GPT-6.1-Sol, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. technology.title: PyTorch 2.15 tackles the 'one bad GPU' problem
technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. Like NumPy, PyTorch supports numerical computing, but it also provides tools for building and training neural networks on CPUs and GPUs. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
science.description: null Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today . "This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added. Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites , which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite. BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9 , Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift. The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace , to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly. Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage. Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile. "The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement.
